thread:
keisha: FYI — StratoAI just pinged about a surprise $22,140 burst charge on their Apr reserved invoice. They say it was caused by cross-region failover during a scheduled infra maintenance on our side. Can finance look? @ajay @maria

ajay: Can you drop the invoice snippet and the usage window? I'll pull the meter lines.

keisha: Paste from their PDF (redacted):
```
Invoice: INV-2026-0427
Reserved commit: $15,000
Burst/overage: $22,140
Charge period: 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30
Note: Peak burst 2026-04-17 02:00-05:00 UTC (cross-region failover)
```

ajay: Thanks. Running a quick metering query now. If the failover caused autoscale bump and cross-region egress, that could be billable but we do have SLA fallback language. @li can you confirm SRE timeline?

li: ops-bot already logged the incident but TL;DR: on 2026-04-17 at ~01:58 UTC we had a rolling maintenance in EU-west that triggered region fallback for 3 hours for a subset of dedicated pools. Autoscale kicked in; traffic shifted to us-east and some jobs hit burst thresholds.

ops-bot: INCIDENT-2026-322: region-failover-eu-west -> us-east. start: 2026-04-17T01:58Z end: 2026-04-17T05:12Z. Affected pools: dedicated-strato-prod-1.

maria: OK appears linked. Contractually we have two relevant items: (1) dedicated SLA: availability target 99.9% with credit for downtime caused by our maintenance windows only if we failed to follow notice/runbook. (2) burst billing policy: bursts in failover scenarios are billable unless we proactively mitigated or offered fallback. Need legal read, but we can consider goodwill.

ajay: My initial recon shows 58% of that $22k is pure compute spike (tokens & GPU hours) and ~12% is cross-region network egress. I can draft a proforma credit.

keisha: Customer is pushing for full waiver — says they had a realtime demo for a client. They're upset. Looking for a quick, empathetic reply.

maria: Proposed: offer a one-time goodwill credit equal to 50% of burst compute charges and waive region-egress fees for that window. That would be roughly: compute credit $6,420, waive egress fees $2,650 -> total ~$9,070. Also include a note about improved maintenance cadence + we will provide a postmortem and a free month of Dedicated Insights retention as goodwill.

sam: @maria I approve the one-time goodwill credit and the retention add-on. Please document the calculation and have @ajay apply the credit to invoice INV-2026-0427. Keep it labeled as "Goodwill: outage-linked credit".

ajay: Will do. Drafting the journal entry now. Sample memo: "Goodwill credit applied for cross-region failover during scheduled maintenance; compute credit $6,420; egress waived $2,650; retention add-on applied (1 month). Total credit $9,070."

keisha: I'll send the customer an empathetic response with timeline and the credit. Thanks team. :heart:

li: I'll post the SRE postmortem in #eng-sre and link it in the customer note.

ops-bot: ACTIONS: 1) Apply credit INV-2026-0427 - ajay. 2) Customer comms - keisha. 3) Postmortem link - li. 4) Legal check (TOS) - maria.

maria: Legal sign-off queued, but we have precedent for goodwill credits here. Closing loop once journal entry is posted.

ajay: Journal entry posted, credit created (CR-2026-778). Applied to INV-2026-0427. I'll update the invoice PDF and push to billing portal.

keisha: Customer confirmed receipt and thanked us for the quick handling. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
